What it is / purpose: One combined prep sheet for enabling a vSphere Supervisor on a VCF workload domain with VCF Networking / VPC + Centralized Transit Gateway. Fill the 'Your value' column. Rows are grouped by Section; the last two sections are an ordered task list and a firewall matrix (its columns are re-labelled in a note at that section).
Notes: Companion to docs/10-supervisor-enablement.md - each Section maps to a section there.

What it is / purpose: This is the VCF 9.0 edition. Activation is per workload domain and Day-N - nothing here happens at bring-up. Several inputs are fixed for the life of the Supervisor (marked IRREVERSIBLE).
Notes: A separate 9.0 / 9.1 edition exists - use the one matching the target build.

What it is / purpose: Created by Albin Qorri (ITQ) as the 'Config Sheet - vSphere Supervisor'. This edition reconciles it with docs/10-supervisor-enablement.md and adds the pre-flight, load-balancer and VKS planning inputs.

What it is / purpose: Advertised CIDRs that allow outside connectivity to VPC workloads. Must be routable and advertised upstream. With Avi in VPC mode this block is ALSO the load-balancer VIP source (Avi IPAM is not used in VPC) - so the Supervisor API VIP and every LoadBalancer Service VIP come from here. Must exist and have free space before activation, and be referenced by the VPC Connectivity Profile.
Notes: docs/10 section 3.3 / 3.4. No documented minimum prefix; size for the VIPs you expect.

What it is / purpose: Private CIDRs for inter-VPC communication within one NSX Project (Tenant). Not routable north-south. One per NSX Project.
Notes: Documented as /16 in both 9.0 and 9.1. Field reports: a /24 makes the deployment hang at the transit-gateway stage rather than fail cleanly - size /16.

What it is / purpose: Private CIDR behind NAT in the VPC. Not routable. Can be the same for each VPC in the same NSX Project.
Notes: 9.0 requirements page: /16.

What it is / purpose: On = workloads/pods SNAT outbound via an external IP (then set 'External IP Block for Default Outbound NAT'). Off = workloads egress with their own private/transit IPs, which must be routable/advertised. Does NOT affect the Supervisor control plane (rides the management network) or the VIP source.
Notes: docs/10 section 3.4 (field-verified). If On but NAT block unset, the profile shows (incompatible).

Item: Attach External IP Block to the VPC Connectivity Profile
What it is / purpose: The block must both exist and be referenced by the Default VPC Connectivity Profile before activation, or the wizard marks the profile (incompatible) and the External IP Blocks table shows 'No items found'. Relaunch the wizard after any NSX/profile change - it caches NSX state.
Notes: docs/10 section 3.4.

What it is / purpose: The first VPC created for the Supervisor lives in the System (default) NSX Project.

What it is / purpose: Needed for every additional workload tenant (new NSX Project / new VCF Automation Org). Private Transit Gateway CIDR and Private CIDR can be re-used.

Supervisor activation requires A load balancer, not specifically Avi. Options on the VPC path: the built-in NSX Edge load balancer (no extra appliance/licence/failure domain) OR Avi. Exclusive: committing the Supervisor to the VCF Native LB rules Avi out for VPCs under it. Choose Avi only for a reason - existing Avi estate, L7 ingress, or a VCFA instance already fronted by it.
Notes: docs/10 section 1.2. If you pick the built-in LB, skip the Avi rows below.

What it is / purpose: Standalone / NSX-native Avi, or VCF-Operations-managed. On 9.0 the manual (standalone) path is the documented one.
Notes: docs/10 section 4.

What it is / purpose: Always the management domain - one set per NSX instance, never per workload domain. 3-node cluster = 4 IPs (one per node + cluster VIP) from the management network. Must be deployed BEFORE Supervisor activation.
Notes: docs/10 section 4.1 / 4.2.

What it is / purpose: Avi Controller 31.1.1 or later.
Notes: docs/10 section 4.2 (documented).

What it is / purpose: Enterprise or Enterprise with Cloud Services. Controller starts in evaluation mode and must be moved off it. A Controller that cannot have licences attached blocks activation as hard as one never deployed.
Notes: 9.1: new subscription licence file format (replaces 25-char serial keys), 90-day grace on the move to 32.1.1 - settle any migration before the deployment day.

Item: Avi - Controller endpoint that goes in the cert SAN
What it is / purpose: Whatever value you give the Supervisor wizard as the Avi Controller endpoint MUST appear in the Controller certificate's SAN. Put both the FQDN and the IP in the SAN (single node: its FQDN+IP; cluster: the VIP FQDN+VIP IP). A self-signed Controller cert is the low-risk path; a private-CA-signed one can hang the deployment with the Avi side silently unapplied.
Notes: docs/10 section 4.4. Standalone Avi only - on VCF-Ops-managed Avi the cert is generated for you.

What it is / purpose: Set the Default-Group correctly BEFORE activation - AKO clones it per Supervisor and will not retro-apply later changes. Set HA mode, max SE count, VS placement (Compact/Distributed), and the vSphere STORAGE POLICY (SEs are VMs - no policy, nowhere to deploy; if not pinned to shared storage, SEs land on host-local datastores and SE HA / host maintenance break).
Notes: docs/10 section 4.3 / 4.5. Storage policy lives on the SE Group, not the Cloud object.

What it is / purpose: You CANNOT deploy the Avi Controller in an ELM vCenter deployment - single vCenter only. Check against your vCenter topology before committing to Avi.
Notes: docs/10 section 4.6 (documented). Decisive in a linked-mode VCF estate.
